summary: Recent M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY who builds embedded controllers and sensor-driven systems, from bare-metal STM32 and Arduino firmware to Jetson edge devices. Built a vision-guided robotic arm with closed-loop visual servoing, ToF-triggered grasping and a WebSocket interface to physical hardware, reaching 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials). Comfortable with Python, C/C++, sensors, actuators and data acquisition.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Built a wearable gesture-recognition glove with ADXL345 accelerometers, Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment; used GitLab for version control.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.

Built a vision-guided robotic pick-and-place system over a three-layer pipeline: Flutter mobile client, Flask-SocketIO edge server, and Jetson+Arduino embedded controller linked by a unified WebSocket fabric.

Used TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms) for visual servoing, with dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper close at 25 mm) via TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping.
Implemented two-link IK on Arduino in C++; drove five servo actuators with range-gated contact detection.
Deployed the Jetson arm bridge as a systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root isolation) with static IP networking for reliable multi-device WebSocket registration.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used FreeRTOS mutexes for task coordination; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance display.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-triggered ADC scan conversions and interrupt-driven sample capture.
Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) with a low-level I2C driver; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
